data.exact_reserve_text: Although the Property team generated a loss in the year it was tempered by favourable development and releases from prior year reserves for the treaty business. US Casualty business has faced difficult market conditions for some years, however, technical rates on our portfolio remain favourable. This book has performed well and it has again been possible to release reserves from prior years. The Syndicate's EL/PL book experienced a loss on the calendar year's result despite being able to achieve rate increases in 2017. The reserves have been subject to a detailed review following the reduction in the UK Personal Injury Discount Rate and, as a consequence, some strengthening was required. The International Casualty and Motor books were also impacted by the reduction in the UK Personal Injury Discount Rate resulting in an increase in the reserves.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a mixed prior year development in 2017. Favourable development and releases were noted for Property (specifically treaty business) and US Casualty lines. However, adverse development led to strengthening of reserves for EL/PL, International Casualty, and Motor books, primarily driven by the reduction in the UK Personal Injury Discount Rate. The overall prior year development resulted in a gross release of GBP 47.148 million.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development calculated from the gross claims development triangle by comparing the current estimate of cumulative claims incurred (last value in each column of the 'Estimated of claims incurred' section) to the estimate at the end of the previous reporting period (values on the previous diagonal) for underwriting years 2011-2015. The '2010 and prior' aggregate column was excluded from the calculation as per instructions.
